extracted.intended_audience: general public, media, policymakers, advocacy groups
extracted.subtask_short: government press release on fake comments
extracted.subtask_description: A state Attorney General press release announcing the results of an investigation into millions of fake public comments submitted to the FCC in a 2017 net neutrality proceeding, describing findings, named perpetrators, and recommended reforms and settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net neutrality definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Net neutrality prohibits broadband providers from blocking, slowing down, or charging companies to prioritize certain content on the internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the policy at issue and frames why the FCC proceeding mattered; used to explain stakes of the rulemaking and why manipulated public input can affect important public policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astroturfing (disguised paid campaigns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disguising an orchestrated, paid campaign as a grassroots effort, to create a false appearance of genuine, unpaid public support — often referred to as astroturfing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterized as deceptive practice used to create the false impression of popular support; the release describes industry-funded lead generators engaging in this practice to influence the FCC's repeal of net neutrality rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of inducements by lead generators (red flag)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead generators used prizes—like gift cards and sweepstakes entries—to lure consumers to their websites and join the campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release identifies such inducements as part of the mechanism for generating comments and as a warning sign that submissions may be inauthentic when combined with other indicators (e.g., mass fabrication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabrication of consumer responses by vendors
rubrics_metrics.description: Nearly every lead generator that was hired to enroll consumers instead simply fabricated consumers’ responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly labeled as fraudulent behavior; an anti-pattern in advocacy campaigns and a principal finding of the investigation showing vendor misconduct rather than legitimate mobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification of fake submissions (scale of fraud)
rubrics_metrics.description: More than 8.5 million fake comments that impersonated real people were submitted to the FCC, more than half a million fake letters were sent to Congress, and nearly 18 million of the more than 22 million comments the FCC received were fake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release uses precise numeric findings to demonstrate scope: 8.5M impersonating real people, 9.3M additional fictitious-identity comments supporting net neutrality (mostly from a single individual using automated software), totaling nearly 18M fake comments; these counts support enforcement and reform recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-campaign vendor fraud (recurring misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three lead generation firms had worked on more than 100 other, unrelated campaigns and, in nearly all of these advocacy campaigns, engaged in fraud, generating more than 1 million fake comments and more than 3.5 million fake digital signatures for other proceedings and officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates systemic vendor misconduct beyond the single proceeding; used to justify broader reforms and oversight rather than one-off remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: obtain valid consent before submitting on someone's behalf
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy groups to take steps to ensure they have obtained valid consent from an individual before submitting a comment or message to the government on their behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recommended reform to prevent impersonation and unauthorized submissions; addresses ethical and legal responsibility of advocacy organizations when acting for individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: hold advocacy groups and vendors accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies and legislatures that manage electronic systems that receive comments and messages to hold advocacy groups and their vendors more accountable for the comments they submit on behalf of individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for procedural and enforcement changes by agencies and legislatures to increase accountability for submissions and intermediaries that deliver bulk comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: strengthen laws to deter deceptive/unauthorized comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawmakers to strengthen laws to deter the submission of deceptive and unauthorized comments to the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legislative reform recommendation aimed at creating clearer deterrence and penalties for fraudulent comment campaigns and impersonation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: adopt technical safeguards against bulk automated submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies to adopt technical safeguards to protect against unauthorized bulk submissions using automation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical and operational reforms (e.g., rate-limiting, verification measures) are recommended to reduce the vulnerability of public comment systems to mass automated or bulk fraudulent submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement outcome requirement for vendors
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements with the lead generators require the companies to adopt comprehensive reforms in future advocacy campaigns and pay more than $4.4 million in penalties and disgorgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement terms combine injunctive relief (operational reforms) with monetary penalties and disgorgement to remediate harm and deter future misconduct; names companies (Fluent, Opt-Intelligence, React2Media) and associates them with approximate counts of fraudulent comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of fake comments as illegal and deceptive
rubrics_metrics.description: The OAG describes the submission of fake comments and impersonation as illegal and deceptive behavior that corrupts the policymaking process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This legal characterization underpins the office's authority to investigate and settle and frames the moral and civic harms used to justify reforms and penalties.
